assumptions: Copper at 20 C, VBUS and GND of the same gauge, both carrying the load current. A mated USB-C pair is taken as 20 mOhm (VBUS + GND). The Pi 5 flags under-voltage below 4.63 V, measured after its input fuse. A USB-C cable is allowed to drop 500 mV on VBUS plus 250 mV on GND at its rated current, so even a compliant cable can lose 0.75 V.

usb.route: Official 27 W supply alone: its 1.2 m, 17 AWG lead (too short to reach)
Official supply + 2 m USB-C extension (22 AWG, one more mated pair)
Official supply + 2 m 240 W (5 A) extension, if it really is 20 AWG
Official supply + 2 m extension of a thin 3 A cable (26 AWG)
5 A PD supply + one 3 m 5 A cable (20 AWG)
5 A PD supply + one 3 m 3 A cable (24 AWG)
iUniker 5.25 V / 4 A, 1.5 m lead (if 18 AWG) + 2 m 240 W extension (20 AWG)
Any PD charger's 5 V / 3 A profile (5.0 V) + a 3 m 240 W cable (20 AWG)
5 V / 2 A camera adapter with its 3 m USB-A to C cable (if 24 AWG)

buck.route: Any PD charger with a 12 V profile + one 3 m 240 W cable (20 AWG), PD step-down board at the Pi
Official supply's 12 V profile + 2 m 240 W extension (20 AWG), PD step-down board at the Pi
